$comment: Options object for a writable Home Assistant entity. Identical to ha_entity's apart from this comment and the controller_options one: HaSwitch subclasses HaEntity, so it parses states the same way and adds Switch + is_writable. Its three keys are spread into HaSwitch.__init__ by main.create_classes — keep in lockstep with the constructor; tests/test_config.py enforces this.

name.$comment: Must reference an existing connector name — enforced by Config at load time, not by the schema

entity_id.$comment: The Home Assistant entity this device mirrors, e.g. 'sensor.grid_import_energy'. A list watches several entities with one device — the last state to arrive wins, so a list is for entities that mean the same thing, not for aggregation.

metric_attributes.$comment: Allowlist of entity attributes to report as metrics. Omit to report every scalar attribute that is not presentation noise (friendly_name, icon, device_class, ...).

energy_attribute.$comment: Which attribute get_total_energy_kwh() reads. Omit it and set energy_unit instead to use the entity's own state — which is the usual shape, since an HA energy sensor's state IS the cumulative reading.

energy_unit.$comment: Wh | kWh | MWh. Declaring it is what makes this entity an energy meter: with neither this nor energy_attribute set, get_total_energy_kwh() reports 0.0 so a thermostat stays harmless in an algorithm that sums every EnergyMeter. Falls back to the entity's own attributes.unit_of_measurement.

controller_options.$comment: How a control command becomes a Home Assistant service call. Declare entity_id (or a per-command target), or the connector drops every command — the device warns about that at startup.

entity_id.$comment: The entity a command targets. Often the same as listener_options.entity_id, but not always: an algorithm may read a power sensor and actuate the switch beside it.

domain.$comment: Default service domain for commands that name none. Omit it and the domain-agnostic 'homeassistant' services are used, which cover lights, switches, fans, scripts, media players and climate alike.

commands.$comment: Command token -> a full service call. A full call rather than {service_on, service_off} because that shape only ever expresses a Switch and dead-ends the moment an algorithm wants climate.set_temperature. 'on'/'off' need no entry: they fall back to homeassistant.turn_on/turn_off. Any OTHER token with no entry is refused with a warning — a service name is never guessed.
